title: Instant Pot Beef & Bean Chili
description: A big, cosy pot of beef, tender beans, and smoky tomato goodness. Made for cooking once and filling the freezer, with everything laid out from the grocery aisle to the last simmer.
shortDescription: Hearty beef, tender beans, and a smoky tomato base. A little prep now, plenty of good dinners later.
imageAlt: A cream bowl of beef and bean chili topped with sour cream, cheddar, and green onions
equipment: Instant Pot with capacity for the full recipe
introNote: Make one full batch with 2 lb of beef. All quantities below are for the whole recipe. Use a cooker large enough to keep this bean chili at or below its half-full limit. Actual yield depends on portion size. Serve with rice or bread for a bigger meal.

items.text: 3 tbsp tomato paste (buy 1 small can or tube)
2 × 15 oz (425 g) cans diced tomatoes, fire-roasted or regular
3 cups (about 710 mL) low-sodium beef broth (buy 1 litre)
3 tbsp chili powder (a mild seasoning blend, not pure ground chile)
2 tsp smoked paprika (+ ½ tsp if using regular tomatoes)
¼ tsp chipotle powder, with regular tomatoes for more smoky heat
1 tsp unsweetened cocoa powder, for depth

prep.title: Chop all the vegetables
prep.text: Dice 2 large onions and 2 bell peppers. Mince 4 garlic cloves. If using, finely dice 1 jalapeño; remove the seeds for less heat. Keep the garlic separate from the onions and peppers.

prep.title: Drain the beans; open the tomatoes
prep.text: Drain and rinse 2 cans kidney beans and 2 cans pinto beans (15 oz / 425 g each). Open 2 cans diced tomatoes and 1 can tomato sauce (15 oz / 425 g each); keep their liquid.

prep.title: Measure the spices
prep.text: In one bowl, measure 3 tbsp chili powder, 2 tsp ground cumin, 2 tsp smoked paprika, and 2 tsp dried oregano. Optional: 1 tbsp brown sugar and/or 1 tsp unsweetened cocoa. With regular tomatoes, add an extra ½ tsp smoked paprika, plus ¼ tsp chipotle powder for extra heat.

prep.title: Gather the full recipe quantities
prep.text: Set out 2 lb (about 900 g) ground beef, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 diced onions, 2 diced bell peppers, 4 minced garlic cloves, 3 tbsp tomato paste, 3 cups broth, 2 cans diced tomatoes with juice, 1 can tomato sauce, 2 cans drained kidney beans, 2 cans drained pinto beans, and the spice bowl. Keep the optional diced jalapeño ready.

prep.title: Get toppings & containers ready
prep.text: If using, slice green onions, chop cilantro, and cut 1–2 limes into wedges. Set out shredded cheddar and sour cream. Have shallow containers ready for chilling and freezing the finished chili.

cookNote: Cook the full recipe once, using all 2 lb of beef and the full ingredient quantities below. Check that the loaded cooker is at or below the half-full limit for beans before pressure cooking.

cooking.title: Brown the beef
cooking.text: Select Sauté and heat 2 tbsp olive oil. Add all 2 lb (about 900 g) lean ground beef, break it into small crumbles, and cook until browned with no pink remaining. Spoon off excess fat if needed.

cooking.title: Soften the vegetables
cooking.text: Add 2 diced large onions, 2 diced bell peppers, and the optional diced jalapeño. Cook, stirring, until softened. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the full prepared spice bowl and cook for another 30 seconds.

cooking.title: Deglaze the pot
cooking.text: Press Cancel. Pour in 3 cups low-sodium beef broth and scrape the bottom thoroughly with a wooden spoon until no browned bits remain stuck. This thin liquid and a clean pot bottom help prevent a burn warning.

cooking.title: Layer in beans & tomatoes
cooking.text: Add 2 cans drained, rinsed kidney beans and 2 cans drained, rinsed pinto beans (each originally 15 oz / 425 g). Spoon 2 cans diced tomatoes with their juice (15 oz / 425 g each), 1 can tomato sauce (15 oz / 425 g), and 3 tbsp tomato paste on top. Do not stir the tomato layer into the bottom. Keep this bean chili at or below the half-full line; if the full recipe exceeds it, use a larger cooker before pressure cooking. Follow the cooker’s minimum thin-liquid requirement.

cooking.title: Pressure cook
cooking.text: Secure the lid, set the valve to Sealing if required by the cooker, and select High Pressure for 20 minutes. The countdown starts after the pot reaches pressure; allow extra time for this full pot to heat up.

cooking.title: Let pressure release naturally
cooking.text: When cooking finishes, turn off Keep Warm and let pressure release fully on its own. Do not quick-release thick chili. Wait until the float valve drops and the lid unlocks; never force it open. The release time varies with the cooker and amount of chili.

cooking.title: Stir, finish & portion
cooking.text: Open the lid facing away from the body and stir everything together, including the tomato paste. Taste and add salt and black pepper as needed. If too thin, use Sauté with the lid off for 5–10 minutes, stirring often; if too thick, add broth a splash at a time. Serve with any cheddar, sour cream, sliced green onions, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges. Transfer the finished chili to shallow containers for chilling and freezing.

notes.title: No fire-roasted tomatoes?
notes.text: Use the same amount of regular canned diced tomatoes. The extra ½ tsp smoked paprika for the whole recipe adds smoke; ¼ tsp chipotle powder adds optional heat. Both are already accounted for in the prep instructions.

notes.title: Bean substitutions
notes.text: Replace any of the four cans with the same size cans of black, navy/white haricot, cannellini, or Romano/cranberry beans. Drain and rinse them. Canned Romano beans are a good fit; fresh flat Romano green beans are a different ingredient. Use cooked canned beans here, not dried beans.

notes.title: Cooker capacity & liquid guidance
notes.text: This is one full batch with 2 lb beef and 3 cups thin broth. Use a cooker large enough for all ingredients to stay at or below the half-full limit for beans; do not assume the full recipe fits a 6-quart cooker. Follow the liquid minimum and fill limits in the cooker’s manual, and allow pressure to release fully naturally. This recipe has not been kitchen-tested.

storage.title: Cool & store
storage.text: Divide into shallow containers and refrigerate or freeze within 2 hours. Keep only the next 2–3 days’ meals in the fridge at 4°C or colder and freeze the rest. Label containers with the date. Do not keep the whole week’s chili in the fridge.

storage.title: Reheat a portion
storage.text: Thaw in the fridge or microwave. Reheat to 74°C / 165°F throughout, stirring so the centre heats evenly. Add a splash of water or broth if needed; only reheat the portion needed.
